title: Modern Warships Admits Copying Alex Jay Brady's Aircraft Design
summary: Artstorm admits Modern Warships copied Alex Jay Brady's ekranoplan design and is seeking a deal, with the ship costing up to $700.

 Cover: GenZHype original graphic. All clips and posts below are embedded from their original sources.

 via kotaku.com 
 Background
 Alex Jay Brady is a concept artist who regularly posts designs to social media, including a 2014 design for an “ekranoplan,” described as a ground effect vehicle that glides just above the water. Modern Warships, a PvP online naval war game developed by Artstorm and published by Gaijin, recently added a vehicle to the game that Brady identified as the basis for their original design.
 The game is freemium, and IGN calculated that buying the specific ship would cost between $50 and $100 in gacha spins, or as much as $700 to buy it outright. Modern Warships is often compared to World of Warships, and its presentation emulates the latter, including promotional artwork styles.
 The timeline
 Oct 5, 2026 
 Alex Jay Brady publicly accuses Modern Warships of plagiarism
 Alex Jay Brady reportedly posted on X that they did not give Modern Warships permission to use their ekranoplan design. Brady noted the game's version was more detailed than their sketches and stated that if the developers had asked and paid, they would have had no issues with the usage. [1] 
 Fair call, and apologies from us. Your design was used as a reference without proper clearance. We’ll contact you directly to make this right.
— MODERN WARSHIPS: Naval Battles (@ModernWarships) Oct 5, 2026 
 Oct 5, 2026 
 Alex Jay Brady demands compensation in follow-up post
 In a subsequent post, Brady allegedly stated that ArtStorm Games used their atomic ekranoplan design without permission or even buying them dinner. Brady reportedly requested that the developers cut them a check, stating they were broke. [4] 
 I did not give @ModernWarships permission to use my ekrano design, but I have to say she's looking great. Much more detailed than my sketches. Honestly if they'd just asked and sent me some $$$$ Id have had zero issue with them using it.
Its not to late to do the right thing guys
— Alex Jay Brady 🥶 (@AlexJayBrady) Oct 5, 2026 
 Oct 5, 2026 
 Modern Warships admitted to using design without clearance
 The official Modern Warships account reportedly responded to Brady on X, admitting that the design was used as a reference without proper clearance. The developer reportedly apologized and stated they would contact Brady directly to make the situation right. [1] 
 Screenshot of kotaku.com, captured Oct 6, 2026. Source [1] 
 Our read of the evidence
 Mostly unverified. The developer’s admission appears only in a social‑media post that was reported by a news outlet, with no independent primary source confirming the statement. The artist’s accusation and follow‑up demand were likewise conveyed through social‑media posts covered by two different outlets, again lacking primary verification. Both sides have spoken on record via their own posts, but the developer’s pledge to contact the artist remains pending, leaving the situation based on reported claims rather than confirmed evidence.
 Our rating counts evidence, not opinions about anyone: events confirmed by a primary source (the person's own post, their official site, a court or government record) weigh most, then how many independent outlets report the story. 
 What happens next
 Artstorm stated it will contact Alex Jay Brady directly to make the situation right, according to the developer's X post.
 Frequently asked
 Did Modern Warships remove the copied design?
 No, according to kotaku.com, Artstorm is attempting to reach a deal with the artist rather than removing the copied design from the game.
 How much does the copied ship cost in Modern Warships?
 According to IGN's math, it would cost between $50 and $100 in gacha spins, or as much as $700 to buy it outright.
 What did Modern Warships say in response to the accusations?
 The developer posted on X that it was a 'fair call' and apologized, stating the design was used as a reference without proper clearance.
 What specific design was copied?
 Alex Jay Brady identified the vehicle as based on their 2014 design for an 'ekranoplan,' a ground effect vehicle that glides just above the water.
 Did Alex Jay Brady say they would have allowed the use for a fee?
 Yes, Brady stated that if the developers had asked and sent money, they would have had zero issues with them using the design.

sources.excerpt:
Warship Game Steals Nonsensical Aircraft Design And Then Tries To Sell It In-Game For $700
 'Your design was used as a reference without proper clearance,' says Artstorm about the replicated ekranoplan
 Artstorm Modern Warships plagiarism War Thunder 
 By
 John Walker 
 Published October 6, 2026
 | 
 Comments ( 2 )
 | 
 𝕏 
 Copied!
 Brady's 2014 design of the floaty ship. © Alex Jay Brady
 Modern Warships , not to be confused with  World of Warships , has come under fire after an independent artist noticed that their ship design had been lifted without permission and added to the game ( thanks IGN ). Artstorm, the developer of the PvP online game of naval war, has admitted to the plagiarism, and rather than removing the copied design, is instead attempting to reach a deal with the artist.
 Alex Jay Brady is a concept artist who regularly posts their designs to social media, including a 2014 design for an “ekranoplan,” a “ground effect” vehicle, a hybrid surface/air ship-cum-plane that glides just above the water via what mechanical engineers call ‘magic.’ The imagined craft is very clearly the basis for the vehicle Modern Warships recently added to the game, and Brady immediately took to their X account to call this out.
 “I did not give @ModernWarships permission to use my ekrano design,” they wrote, “but I have to say she’s looking great. Much more detailed than my sketches.” They add, “Honestly if they’d just asked and sent me some $$$ I’d have had zero issues with them using it. It’s not too late to do the right thing guys.”
 I did not give @ModernWarships permission to use my ekrano design, but I have to say she's looking great. Much more detailed than my sketches. Honestly if they'd just asked and sent me some $$$$ Id have had zero issue with them using it.
Its not to late to do the right thing guys https://t.co/luxN8zsU5f pic.twitter.com/E2K7z3rE9i 
 — Alex Jay Brady 🥶 (@AlexJayBrady) October 5, 2026 
 IGN asked Brady for more details and was told, “For me the design is the same, with a few minor differences… But as there was never a swing wing ekranoplan carrier (for good reason) and every detail aside from that is carried over from my design, it seems cut and dried.” They added that much of the design is non-functional, including that “the engines wash across the deck, the planes take off backward, not into the wind, I just didn’t know anything about the subject when building it and they cloned all those mistakes wholesale.”
 Rather peculiarly, Artstorm responded to Brady in public on X with a full admission. “Fair call,” the developer posted, “and apologies from us. Your design was used as a reference without proper clearance. We’ll contact you directly to make this right.”
 Fair call, and apologies from us. Your design was used as a reference without proper clearance. We’ll contact you directly to make this right.
 — MODERN WARSHIPS: Naval Battles (@ModernWarships) October 5, 2026 
 It certainly doesn’t help that buying the ship in the freemium game is enormously expensive.  IGN ‘s math says it would cost between $50 and $100 in gacha spins, or as much as $700 to buy it outright. And while  Modern Warships isn’t exactly overwhelmed with players, there’s a few hundred people in the game at any one time.
 It’s also rather striking how much  Modern Warships ‘ presentation seems to emulate the far more mammoth World of Warships , right down to those familiar fans of ships arranged in promotional artwork.
 © Wargaming © Artstorm Given that Modern Warships is published by Gaijin, of War Thunder fame, you’d think there’d be some slightly better measures put in place here. Hopefully Brady will get their bag, but other artists might well want to take a look through the game to see if they’re owed anything.
